  • Nottoway↗Present community government and historical regional connection
    Connection & source
    Present community government and historical regional connection

    Virginia's community account identifies the Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia as descending from the larger historical Nottoway community and describes its community house and interpretive center in Capron, Virginia. This gives the broader Nottoway entry an initial Virginia route through a named present community. Inspection: Read the substantive historical/community paragraphs, especially the distinction between the larger historical community and present tribe and the Capron community-facility paragraph. Limits: This source concerns Nottoway Indian Tribe of Virginia. Do not merge it with the separate Cheroenhaka (Nottoway) government. The entry is a broad directory access point; no boundary or exclusive historical-state range is asserted. This geographic record is not an independent federal-recognition review.

    Contemporary state community description with historical Virginia context, inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Pamunkey↗Present community / ancestral reservation connection
    Connection & source
    Present community / ancestral reservation connection

    The Tribe locates the Pamunkey community along the Pamunkey River adjacent to King William County, Virginia. Actual opening geography and continuing-residence paragraphs were read. This is a specific community connection, not all Virginia, a precise parcel boundary or an independent finding on every historical/legal claim in the page.

    Undated tribal account inspected October 21, 2026. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Powhatan↗Historical alliance / regional connection
    Connection & source
    Historical alliance / regional connection

    The NPS biography places Powhatan’s historical alliance in Tidewater Virginia. This is a route to the wider historical political grouping, whose constituent communities retained distinct identities; it is not a claim that one present nation occupies all Virginia. Inspection: Actual opening, line 42, and discussion of the alliance’s coastal Virginia geography. Personal-life reconstructions and population totals are not adopted.

    Late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
